search_query: Red Lion Mill End Road Cherry Hinton Cambridge pub CAMRA
description: A sixteenth-century village inn on Mill End Road forms the heart of Cherry Hinton social life, recently reopened after refurbishment under Greene King's Hive franchise. Inside, a single room splits into distinct drinking areas around a central fireplace, with an extension hosting occasional live music. A large covered garden draws families and dog walkers, while Sky and TNT screens show Premier League and international fixtures. The Greene King menu runs from weekday lunch deals to Sunday roasts, burgers and pizzas, with pool, darts, quiz nights and karaoke rounding out a classic community local.
notes: Sources: CAMRA Cambridge (pubs.cambridge-camra.org.uk id=1828), camra.org.uk WhatPub, theredlioncherryhinton.co.uk. Original building dates from 16th century; reopened June 2023 as Hive pub. New licensees April 2025. Queue already has website and short description.

search_query: Waggon and Horses Margett Street Cottenham Cambridge pub CAMRA
description: Tucked away on a quiet Cottenham back street, this small free house reopened in November 2024 after years closed through the pandemic, following a bright refurbishment under new independent owners. A café-style atmosphere serves cakes and savoury snacks alongside eight keg taps and two rotating real ales from local brewers such as Papworth and Milton. A private rear courtyard offers outdoor seating. Regular events include darts on Monday and Wednesday evenings, board games on Mondays, poker on Wednesdays and a women's darts night on Sundays. CAMRA named it Most Improved Rural Pub 2025.
notes: Sources: CAMRA Cambridge (id=1680), camra.org.uk WhatPub, inapub.co.uk (TNT Sports listed). No official website found. Registered as The Waggon Pub LLP June 2025. Rear courtyard rather than full beer garden.

search_query: Admiral High Street Over Cambridge CB24 pub CAMRA
description: Standing at the centre of Over village, this Victorian local was formerly the Admiral Vernon before Barry and Jane Arliss and family bought it free of tie and reopened it in July 2024 after a full interior, patio and garden refurbishment. Drinking areas wrap in an L-shape around a wood-panelled bar, with steps up to one room and a larger space leading to a rear patio and beer garden. CAMRA lists freshly produced food with daily specials and Sunday roasts, Adnams Ghost Ship plus Brewpoint seasonal beers and guest ales sold as tasting flights. Three indoor screens show sport, with quiz nights and a Friday meat raffle.
notes: Sources: CAMRA Cambridge (id=1648), camra.org.uk WhatPub, overvillage.co.uk reopening article, capturingcambridge.org history. Dogs welcome outside only. Square site is ordering page; no dedicated pub website. Phone also listed as 01954 232357 on some aggregators.

search_query: Sun Inn Waterbeach Chapel Street Cambridge CB25 pub CAMRA
description: Overlooking Waterbeach village green, this traditional local lives by a philosophy of good beer and good music. A cosy lounge to the right is dominated by a huge fireplace surrounded by rustic bric-a-brac, while the simply appointed public bar with its woodblock floor stays lively. Seating spreads to the front, a side smoking area and a sun-trap rear garden. An annual beer and music festival runs over the early May bank holiday, with live music at the weekend event and gigs in an upstairs function room. Changing guest ales often include local brews and dark beers. Long-serving licensee Helen stood down in September 2025; the pub reopened after redecoration in October.
notes: Sources: CAMRA Cambridge (id=1669, listed as Sun Inn), camra.org.uk WhatPub, useyourlocal.com, pubsgalore.co.uk. OSM name 'The Sun' matches Sun Inn. No official website; Facebook group exists. Address 7 Chapel Street CB25 9HR.

search_query: White Horse Waterbeach Green Side Cambridge pub CAMRA Lapen Inns
description: Opposite Waterbeach village green, this split-level coaching inn was saved from redevelopment and relaunched in February 2025 by Lapen Inns, the Nepalese hospitality group behind the Old Crown in Girton and Corner House in Cambridge. Two connected bars combine a lower level with pool table and a higher restaurant area, with a large rear garden and log fires in winter. The menu pairs British pub classics and mixed grills with authentic Nepalese dishes such as bhutuwa chicken and Pokhareli fish curry. Wednesday quiz nights, live sports, and dog-friendly spaces including covered terraces make it a renewed community hub on Greenside.
notes: Sources: whitehorsepub.co, lapeninns.com, CAMRA East Anglia (id=86466), Cambridge News Feb 2025 reopening article. Queue lists old Facebook URL; current official site is whitehorsepub.co. CAMRA phone 01223 505053 may be outdated.

search_query: Bell Inn Balsham West Wickham Road Cambridge pub CAMRA
description: A popular community two-bar pub on West Wickham Road, purchased in spring 2018 by a local resident after years as a Greene King house and now run independently. The public bar offers a jukebox, pub games and television, while the wood-panelled lounge suits diners and drinkers alike with tasty homemade food at affordable prices, Sunday roasts and occasional food vans on Mondays. Changing ales always include a mild or dark beer, with locally produced ciders often available. A large rear beer garden features cosy sheds for wet weather, and a quiz runs on the last Tuesday of each month. New licensees took over in September 2025.
notes: Sources: CAMRA Cambridge (id=1642), camra.org.uk WhatPub, thebellinnbalsham.com menu PDF, useyourlocal.com. CAMRA Dark Beer Pub of the Year 2022. Address 2 West Wickham Road CB21 4DZ.

search_query: White Hart Country Inn Fulbourn Balsham Road Cambridge pub CAMRA
description: Set on Balsham Road in the picturesque village of Fulbourn, this family-run venue reopened in November 2025 following a major refurbishment as a premium steak and fish restaurant under operator Neil Robertson, who also runs the Hat and Rabbit in the same village under Greene King Pub Partners. The spacious interior is mainly laid out for dining, with a small snug area closest to the bar. Menus focus on farm-to-fork steaks, fresh fish from UK fishmongers and traditional Sunday roasts, with ample customer parking. Sister pub to the Tram Depot in Cambridge. CAMRA notes real ale is not yet available and letting rooms are not currently in use.
notes: Sources: thewhitehartfulbourn.co.uk, CAMRA Cambridge (id=1780), Greene King pubs news on £375k refurbishment. Previously marketed as country inn with B&B; CAMRA Nov 2025 states rooms not in use and no cask ale yet. Dog friendly per website.

search_query: Three Horseshoes Comberton South Street Cambridge pub CAMRA
description: Hanging baskets front this red-tiled village pub at the heart of Comberton, where a long low-ceilinged main bar retains exposed beams hinting at its former multi-room layout. A separate garden and family room opens onto a large rear garden with flower borders and children's play equipment, making it a draw for local families. Three changing cask ales feature regional and national breweries, often including Oakham, alongside two darts teams and a crib team. Food includes Saturday morning breakfasts, regular meals and Fish and Chip Fridays from 5–8pm, replacing the former Cambridge Fish Bar van. New licensees arrived in August 2023.
notes: Sources: CAMRA Cambridge (id=1672), camra.org.uk WhatPub, useyourlocal.com (pool, darts, big screen), comberton.org village blog on Fish and Chip Fridays. Official website threehorseshoescomberton.co.uk is minimal. Private licensee accommodation on site, not guest rooms.

search_query: Queen Edith Wulfstan Way Cambridge Individual Pubs CAMRA
description: Cambridge's first purpose-built pub in roughly thirty years when it opened in 2015, this Milton Brewery sibling on Wulfstan Way wears mock-Georgian design inside and out. The larger bar to the left of the entrance has large windows on two sides and a wood-burning stove, while wall clocks are set to seven minutes past five—the moment Boris Johnson announced the first Covid lockdown. The second bar has wooden booths down one side. Regular and changing Milton beers plus guest ales are served, with a partly covered front outdoor area. Kitchen food runs Wednesday to Sunday; Monday quiz nights. Cambridgeshire CAMRA Pub of the Year 2022.
notes: Sources: CAMRA Cambridge (id=27985), camra.org.uk WhatPub, individualpubs.co.uk/queenedith, Cambridge Independent CAMRA POTY 2022 article. Run by Jutt Bloxam per press coverage.

search_query: White Horse Oakington Longstanton Road Cambridge pub CAMRA
description: A pleasant two-bar village local on Longstanton Road where the left-hand room functions as a restaurant serving popular British cuisine and the right-hand drinking bar retains bare-board floors, plain bench seating, an open fire and framed photos of old Oakington. Patio doors lead to an attractive large garden with front tables too. Regular events include darts on winter Mondays, poker on Tuesdays, pétanque on summer Wednesdays and quiz night on Thursdays. Greene King IPA is a regular beer with changing guests. A two-bedroom cottage is available for holiday lets. Registered Asset of Community Value and a popular village meeting place.
notes: Sources: CAMRA Cambridge (id=1684), camra.org.uk WhatPub, whitehorse-oakington.co.uk/about-us. Address 28 Longstanton Road CB24 3AB. Live music listed on pub website facilities. Holiday cottage accommodation, not hotel rooms.

search_query: John Barleycorn Moorfield Road Duxford Cambridge pub CAMRA
description: Built in 1660 as a coaching house, this thatched-roof inn on Moorfield Road in Duxford retains many original features within a single food-led bar where tables serve diners yet a distinct area welcomes drinkers only. Up to four real ales and Weston's Old Rosie cider are available, with a car park and garden to the rear and front drinking tables. En-suite accommodation in a block at the rear is scheduled to restart in March 2026 alongside a new children's play area. The pub closed in July 2025 and reopened under new Red Comb Pubs management on 4 December 2025, two miles from Imperial War Museum Duxford.
notes: Sources: CAMRA Cambridge (id=6518), camra.org.uk WhatPub, visitcambridge.org (alternate phone 01223 691411 and email hello@johnbarleycornpub.co.uk). Accommodation restarting March 2026 per CAMRA. Queue website johnbarleycorn.co.uk returned too-short scrape.

search_query: White Horse Inn Swavesey Market Street Cambridge pub CAMRA
description: Occupying a fine old building in Swavesey's former market area, this historic seventeenth-century inn was long regarded as one of Cambridgeshire's finest community pubs. The classic public bar features polished floor tiles, beamed ceiling, wood panelling and an elevated fireplace, with later additions including a lounge dining area, pool and function rooms, and a large garden with play equipment. Locally sourced home-cooked food ranged from sandwiches and pizzas to hearty mains and Sunday lunch. CAMRA Community Rural Pub of the Year 2020. The pub closed on 25 March 2026 when the Bonson family ceased trading; a local campaign seeks to save and reopen it.
notes: Sources: CAMRA Cambridge (id=1685), camra.org.uk WhatPub (closed long-term 25/03/2026), savethewhitehorseinn.co.uk campaign, useyourlocal.com (temporarily closed). Queue website thewhitehorseswavesey.com DNS failed. Features describe pre-closure operation. Campaign site is not official pub website.

search_query: Golden Ball Inn Boxworth High Street Cambridge CB23 pub CAMRA
description: A sixteenth-century thatched country inn on Boxworth High Street, transformed by a major renovation that replaced a flat bar roof with a pitched vault draped in Latin-script tapestries, added a conservatory leading to patio and an impressive garden, and attached a ten-room detached hotel annex. Heavily food-led with a strong reputation, the venue also maintained a large bar area serving Brewpoint regulars. Wells and Co operated the pub until it closed at the end of June 2025. CAMRA reported in March 2026 that work is underway with the aim of reopening in May 2026 under new management, though it remains closed at time of research.
notes: Sources: CAMRA Cambridge (id=1739, long-term closed), camra.org.uk WhatPub, wellsandco.com tenancy listing, CAMRA pub news April 2026 (reopening May planned). Address 35 High Street CB23 4LY. Queue has_description=true; features reflect pre-closure operation.

search_query: White Horse Foxton High Street Cambridge CB22 pub CAMRA
description: A straightforward village local on Foxton High Street with a U-shaped layout where one slightly raised arm serves as a games area with a pool table. A pétanque court sits in the garden behind this friendly warm pub, which changed hands in January 2020 and serves three changing cask ales. Food is available regularly including Friday fish and chips and Sunday lunch, with terrestrial TV and football coverage. Reviews praise a clean atmosphere, welcoming staff and reasonably priced roasts. Foxton railway station is roughly six hundred metres away, making it accessible for walkers exploring the Cam valley villages south of Cambridge.
notes: Sources: CAMRA Cambridge (id=1835), camra.org.uk WhatPub, useyourlocal.com reviews and facilities. Address 45 High Street Foxton CB22 6RP. No official website found; distinguish from White Horse Oakington and Waterbeach.

search_query: Bank Micropub High Street Willingham Cambridge CB24 CAMRA
description: Opened in late 2012 within a former village bank on Willingham High Street, this single-room micropub centres on a short bar rescued from a closed Cambridge pub, with walls decorated in photos of local interest. Beers pour direct from cask, KeyKeg or keg, alongside a well-stocked fridge of cans and bottles and a range of still, kegged and bottled ciders. There is no kitchen, but changing food vans park nearby on Saturday evenings from 5–8pm. Closed Sunday and Monday, the Bank offers a warm welcome where casual visitors are quickly drawn into local conversation—a social hub that arguably serves the village better than banking ever did.
notes: Sources: CAMRA Cambridge (id=7409), camra.org.uk WhatPub, thebankmicropub.co.uk/find.php. Address 9 High Street Willingham CB24 5ES. Website scrape failed (too short). Opening hours differ slightly between CAMRA and pub site; CAMRA hours used.
